slides.title:
Decentralized Role-Leasing
IoT Protocol
slides.body:
A reproducible simulator for hierarchical agricultural sensor networks

Student: [Name]    Registration: [Number]
Institution: [Institution]
Department: [Department]    Guide: [Name]
slides.notes: Introduce this as a software simulation of coordination in agricultural IoT. The central contribution is selecting temporary role holders using recursive capability, migration costs, and lease rules. The supplied folder does not identify the student, institution, department, or guide, so replace the marked fields before presenting. The implementation and stored experiments support statements about this model, not a deployed farm network. Allow about 18 minutes for slides 1–33 and use the appendix for questions.

slides.title: Project overview
body: Python simulation of a fixed logical hierarchy over a physical multi-hop mesh
100 nodes, 10 subnets, 3 networks, 1 internetwork by default
Four role labels at 14 scopes produce 56 required assignments
Users: researchers and students comparing coordination policies
slides.notes: Explain the distinction between a role and a scope. A gateway role exists separately for each subnet, each network, and the internetwork. Candidates are immediate children: nodes within a subnet, subnets within a network, and networks at the root. The system measures service availability and communication costs under changing conditions. Anomaly detection, health monitoring, and discoverability are role labels and scores. The code does not implement their application payload services. Transition to why reassignment is useful.

slides.title: Problem statement
body: Fixed role holders may remain assigned after their energy or connectivity deteriorates
Global coordination creates a dependency on a controller in the modeled baselines
Frequent reassignment consumes communication energy and can cause instability
The engineering problem is balancing capability improvement against switching cost
slides.notes: Present this as the problem investigated by the project rather than a claim about every IoT deployment. Node energy and link quality affect both suitability and communication. Choosing the highest current score at every step can produce unnecessary churn. Keeping every original holder can leave roles unavailable. The simulator creates a controlled way to compare those policies on the same initial world and event schedule. Ask the panel to judge the mechanism and the evidence under the stated abstraction.

slides.title: Motivation and objectives
body: Preserve useful role availability when nodes fail or conditions change
Reuse the same role semantics across hierarchy levels
Account for routed control traffic, data traffic, and endpoint energy
Make experiments repeatable with seeded inputs and replayable events
slides.notes: The specification motivates agricultural networks with distributed, potentially solar-powered devices. In implementation, this becomes a deterministic experiment framework. Its objectives are observable: capability refresh, temporary assignments, failure recovery, and separate communication counters. Solar harvesting is a later implemented extension. Do not suggest that the project contains real agricultural sensor readings or hardware measurements. The hierarchy is an input assumption, so automatic clustering is outside the current objectives.

slides.title: Implemented comparison policies
slides.notes: Read each row as the exact policy in this codebase. The hierarchical baseline chooses a seeded random fixed controller and random reachable eligible holders, retaining them until failure. Centralized instead uses a fixed controller selected by normalized degree and capability-based reassignment. Static stops policy updates after initialization. Dynamic has local control sources and immediately selects the best reachable score. Proposed adds cost-aware optional migration and leases. These are custom model baselines, not implementations of LEACH, RPL, or another named networking standard.

slides.title: Proposed solution
body: Compute a role capability vector for each online node
Aggregate child vectors bottom-up through the logical hierarchy
Grant one temporary lease for each role and scope
Migrate only when the candidate clears utility and hysteresis checks
Route control exchanges and sensor load through the physical mesh
slides.notes: Describe the mechanism as several cooperating modules. The capability calculation says who is suitable. The protocol engine decides whether a change is justified. The lease state machine records who currently holds a role. The router makes communication success and energy visible. The system is decentralized in modeled control-source selection, but one Mesa model executes the simulation in a single process. It does not implement distributed consensus or independent devices exchanging real packets.

slides.title: Technology stack and tradeoffs
slides.notes: These responsibilities are visible in imports and code. Mesa supplies agent identity and a model clock, while transitions enforces legal state changes. NumPy supplies seeded random generators and numeric operations. Pandas exports and aggregates metrics. Matplotlib produces plots. SciPy is used for t intervals by the study analyzer, but requirements.txt does not declare it. The original specification mentions SimPy and NetworkX, but the active simulator uses neither. Adjacency dictionaries and a custom heap-based router implement the graph behavior. These rationales are architectural interpretations, not recorded author interviews. Environment verification found that Mesa 3.5.1 conflicts with assigning a string to model.scenario. Short simulations work with Mesa 3.3.1. Pin and test a compatible Mesa version before the live demo. NetworkX is a Mesa dependency in this environment, but this project does not use it directly for topology or routing.
rows: Explicit legal node and lease states

slides.title: System architecture
slides.notes: Follow the diagram from the CLI or study runner into RoleSimulationModel. Configuration and the event schedule define the world. Topology creates positions and the physical adjacency map. EntityHierarchy maps the logical organization. Capability refresh feeds ProtocolEngine, which owns leases and uses NetworkRouter for grants, renewals, and migration. Sensor traffic uses that same router. MetricsRecorder reads the resulting state and counters. The experiment layer exports CSV and PNG, while the study layer additionally writes compressed NumPy time series. The diagram represents runtime dependencies, not separate servers.

slides.title: Project structure
slides.notes: The active implementation is the simulation package plus nodes.py. The standalone placer.py creates a map and visualization but the active runner directly calls create_topology rather than loading network_map.csv. The patent-study folder contains execution, aggregation, and stored evidence. Older HANDOFF.md and Roadmap.md describe a hierarchy.py monolith that is absent from this folder. FINAL_SPRINT_PLAN.md explicitly supersedes that direction. Use the current package names when explaining code and avoid repeating old lease counts or incomplete status from the handoff.
rows: Node attributes, capability, online / failed state

slides.title: Physical mesh and logical hierarchy
slides.notes: Read the left chain as candidate membership, not radio links. The default subnet distribution is 4, 3, and 3. A container is available if at least one descendant node is online. Its representative is the first available descendant in stored order, not necessarily its best gateway. On the physical side, distance creates undirected edges and normalized degree supplies centrality. Positive intercluster spacing also inserts nearest bridge links between adjacent clusters. These long-range links are an abstraction and can exceed the nominal communication range. No hierarchy relationship automatically provides a route.

slides.title: Simulation tick workflow
slides.notes: Mesa advances the step count and invokes the model step. Apply scheduled events first and fail depleted nodes. Refresh capabilities before policy decisions so failure and degradation influence selection. Mark affected scopes if configured, then update leases and migrations. Harvest solar energy after protocol decisions and before sensor traffic. Route sensor and optional backhaul traffic, fail newly depleted nodes, refresh capabilities again, and record metrics. This ordering matters: a node recharged during harvesting can rejoin, while a missing lease may only be assigned at a later policy update.

slides.title: Node capability scoring
body: Gateway = 0.40E + 0.35Q + 0.25C
Anomaly detection = health monitoring = 0.50E + 0.50H
Discoverability = 0.34E + 0.33Q + 0.33H
Example: E=.9, H=.8, Q=.7, C=.6 gives gateway .755
Failed nodes contribute zero capability
slides.notes: Define E as normalized battery energy, H as health, Q as node link quality, and C as normalized initial degree. ROLE_WEIGHTS in nodes.py is the single source of truth. Gateway capability in the example is .36 plus .245 plus .15, which is .755. Both anomaly detection and health monitoring produce .85 because their weight definitions are identical. Discoverability produces .801. Scores are bounded to [0,1]. A positive capability does not guarantee a route, which is why selection also checks reachability. No learned model or classifier appears here.

slides.title: Node lifecycle: online, failure, and recovery
slides.notes: The real NodeAgent state machine has exactly two states: online and failed. Construction starts online. A scheduled fail event or the coordinator detecting zero energy invokes fail(). Both paths remove node availability and trigger graph invalidation. Scheduled recover events invoke recover(). Only nodes tracked in _energy_depleted_node_ids can rejoin automatically after solar charging reaches minimum_energy_reserve. Solar charging alone does not repair an explicit scheduled failure. Energy and link degradation update attributes rather than introducing extra states. Role ownership lives in ProtocolEngine.assignments, outside this state machine. A node may be online without holding any role, and becoming online does not guarantee a lease or route. Explain this distinction before discussing role selection.

slides.title: Recursive capability aggregation
body: weighted_aggregate() uses normalized non-negative child weights
Missing child weights default to 1.0, so the default is a mean
Subnet vectors feed network vectors, then the internetwork vector
Failed children remain in the denominator with zero capability
Unequal child populations make a mean of means differ from a global node mean
slides.notes: For child gateway scores .8 and .6 with weights 1 and 3, the aggregate is (.8 + 1.8) / 4 = .65. Empty children return a zero vector. Invalid negative weights or a nonpositive total raise an error. Refresh starts with all leaf vectors and updates each parent in dependency order. The default root gives equal weight to networks despite their 4/3/3 subnet counts. That is a hierarchy weighting choice, not a population-weighted global average. Recomputing from children keeps the function deterministic and independent of previous aggregate values.

slides.title: Selection and assignment
body: Candidates are immediate children of the requested scope
Filter unavailable entities and unreachable representatives
Choose maximum capability with a stable string-ID tie break
Send LEASE_GRANT before creating the active lease
Store leases in dict[(role, scope)] to enforce one holder per pair
slides.notes: Explain _select_for_role and _assign together. A scope needs a control source and at least one reachable candidate. The proposed initial assignment is capability-based and does not deduct migration cost because no holder is being replaced. The hierarchical policy instead uses seeded random choice. A failed grant leaves the role unassigned. A successful grant creates a Lease and activates it. The tuple-keyed dictionary gives direct access to each role/scope assignment. Multiple roles may share a holder because the code has no capacity limit or exclusivity across different role keys.

slides.title: Role assignment at the subnet level
slides.notes: This is an actual initial proposed-policy snapshot from SimulationConfig(seed=42). At scope network_0_subnet_0, immediate child nodes 0 through 9 compete. The control source is physical node 0. The engine filters unavailable or unreachable representatives and ranks known capability. The initial gateway lease holder is node 4. All four roles happen to select node 4 in this subnet, but the code evaluates each role independently and does not require that coincidence. Displayed node scores are sampled just after initialization and include the tiny control-energy effects of initial grants. Container scores were refreshed before those grants. The numbers illustrate the stored assignment, not a new benchmark. A failed grant would leave the role unassigned.

slides.title: Role assignment at the network level
slides.notes: At network_0, candidates are the subnet entities network_0_subnet_0 through network_0_subnet_3. They carry aggregated capability vectors, rather than being evaluated as individual nodes. The observed gateway lease selects subnet 3. The model represents that container physically through node 30, its first available descendant. This representative is not necessarily the subnet gateway selected by a different lease. Anomaly detection, health monitoring, and discoverability choose subnet 0 in this snapshot. Stress that the holder ID is a subnet string at this level. The scope representative still sends the abstract grant over the physical mesh.

slides.title: Role assignment at the internetwork level
slides.notes: At the internetwork scope, the candidates are network_0, network_1, and network_2. Their capability vectors aggregate their child subnets. In the seed-42 initial proposed run, network_2 holds all four root roles. Its first available descendant is physical node 70. Gateway scores for networks 1 and 2 are close, so show six decimal places to avoid an apparent rounded tie. The max selection tie-breaker is string ID only when score values tie. The root selects a network entity, not a single node across the entire deployment. There is one root scope, so this contributes four of the total 56 role assignments.

slides.title: Lease lifecycle and epoch handling
slides.notes: The transitions library prohibits illegal jumps. New leases start pending and activate. Renewal temporarily enters renewing and updates timing before returning active. Migration enters migrating and replaces holder, epoch, and timing in the same lease object. Expiry or invalidation ends availability. Duration in proposed is 10 + capability times 90 by default, so a .8 score gives 82 ticks and renewal becomes due at 57.4 ticks, checked on integer ticks. Epochs advance every 20 ticks. Default behavior regrants assignments, while retention updates existing epoch labels in place. This is an in-process fencing model, not a distributed stale-message rejection protocol.

slides.title: Cost-aware migration
body: Cost = α·2 + β·state_transfer + γ·route_cost·Econtrol + δ·disruption
Candidate utility = capability − λ·cost
Migrate only if best utility > current capability + Δ
Unreachable transfer routes have infinite cost and are excluded
slides.notes: The cost terms are deterministic estimates. The control-message term is fixed at two, while _migrate sends one modeled MIGRATE exchange from the scope source to the new holder. Thus the utility estimate and actual charged control energy are related but distinct models. With route cost 6 and default control energy .00001, cost is .020 + .025 + .0006 + .050 = .0956. Candidate score .88 gives utility .87044. Against current .80 and delta .05, migration passes. A .85 candidate gives .84044 and fails. Optional cooldown and adaptive hysteresis can further restrict changes.

slides.title: Routing algorithm and example
body: Dijkstra minimizes sum of edge costs using a min-heap
Usable quality = base edge quality × min(endpoint link qualities)
Edge cost = 1 + 4 × (1 − quality)
Example: direct quality .2 costs 4.2, two quality .9 hops cost 2.8
Cache routes by source and invalidate after topology-affecting events
slides.notes: This algorithm prefers the two-hop route in the example even though it uses more hops. A link at or below minimum_link_quality is excluded. Failed nodes lose incident usable links. Sorted neighbors and a numerical tolerance stabilize equal-cost behavior. Source equals destination returns a zero-hop successful route. A missing path returns None and increments a delivery-failure counter when a message is offered. Cache invalidation happens on failure, recovery, link degradation, and depletion. The router stores explicit path tuples for all reachable destinations, so path materialization adds overhead beyond the textbook Dijkstra bound.

slides.title: Communication and energy accounting
body: Count logical messages separately from message-hop transmissions
Each hop charges both transmitter and receiver
Transmit = Ebase × [1 + w × (distance / range)^p]
Receive = Ebase, with data and control using different base costs
Failed routing counts an offered item, while no route means no hop energy
slides.notes: Default data energy is .00005 per endpoint and control energy .00001. Distance weight defaults to zero, while the stored clustered study uses weight one and exponent two. A zero-hop message succeeds without communication energy. Accounting records requested modeled costs even when battery depletion clamps the actual battery at zero, so communication energy and residual battery loss are not interchangeable conservation totals. Explicit degradation and harvested energy also change batteries. The model omits retransmissions, interference, sensing, CPU work, and idle consumption. All energy values use normalized units rather than joules.

slides.title: Solar harvesting and migration gate
body: Seeded node harvest = configured rate × uniform(.5, 1.5)
Battery capacity caps accepted harvest and records curtailed energy
Energy-depleted nodes rejoin after reaching the reserve threshold
Optional gate compares projected reserve benefit with transfer energy + margin
Failure replacement bypasses the optional migration gate
slides.notes: Each node has a constant harvest rate for the entire run, with a separate seeded generator to avoid changing topology randomness. The projection uses battery plus horizon times harvest minus observed average communication use, then clamps capacity and subtracts essential reserve. Default horizon is 500 steps and margin is .01. Container reserve projections average available descendants. The gate does not replace capability and migration-cost ranking. It acts after hysteresis and applies only to optional migrations. This is a simple extrapolation without daylight or weather cycles, and the stored results must determine whether it actually helps.

slides.title: Failure detection and role reassignment
slides.notes: Follow the upper path for an unavailable holder. ProtocolEngine tracks when the holder became unavailable and honors detection_delay_steps before invalidating. Container availability uses any online descendant, so one failed descendant does not necessarily invalidate a container lease. The engine removes an invalid lease and calls _assign to select a reachable replacement. Grant success activates the new lease and records recovery time when a pending recovery exists. No reachable candidate or failed communication leaves the role unassigned and a later step retries. The optional solar migration gate only controls discretionary migration and is not invoked for this emergency assignment path. Role availability and route reachability are related but separate checks.

slides.title: Data flow and persistence
slides.notes: Distinguish sensor-item delivery from hierarchical backhaul. Every currently online node offers one sensor item to its subnet gateway. The sensor delivery metric counts that first-leg success. When backhaul is enabled, successful subnets produce one aggregate to a network gateway, and active networks produce one aggregate to the internetwork gateway. Those aggregate deliveries have separate counters and do not redefine sensor-item delivery as end-to-end root receipt. Metrics accumulate in memory and export to CSV, PNG, and study NPZ files. There is no database, web API, or persistent server in this project.

slides.title: Internal interfaces and failure handling
slides.notes: These are Python calls in one process, not HTTP endpoints. Configuration validates finite values, dimensions, ranges, and lease settings. Event construction rejects unsupported kinds and invalid degradation values. Model initialization rejects unknown node references and events beyond the configured horizon. Routing rejects invalid endpoint IDs but returns None for unavailable or disconnected endpoints. Lease transitions reject invalid lifecycle operations. Security is currently about input validation and state consistency. Authentication, authorization, encryption, and protection from malicious IoT nodes are absent because no actual network service is exposed.

slides.title: Actual application outputs
body: The application runs through a command line
Generated CSVs contain run summaries, time series, migrations, and loads
Stored study plots visualize four scenarios and four study arms
No graphical application screens exist in the supplied project
slides.notes: Show the genuine stored figure on this slide as an application output, not a product UI screenshot. Its panels come from patent-study/results_20000/sensor_delivery.png. The study compares A hierarchical without harvest, B proposed without harvest, C proposed with moderate harvest, and D proposed with harvest plus the gate. These labels differ from the five generic CLI policies. Do not invent a dashboard. For a live demonstration, use the next slide and open the generated summary and migration CSV. The plot represents simulated cumulative sensor delivery under the documented study setup.

slides.title: Demonstration workflow
body: 1  Run a short matched experiment with seed 42
2  Compare proposed and hierarchical under node_failures
3  Inspect summary.csv for delivery and role continuity
4  Inspect migration and time-series CSVs around failure / recovery
5  Use the full study only when explaining long-horizon findings
slides.notes: Suggested command: python -m simulation.main --seed 42 --steps 100 --scenarios node_failures --protocols hierarchical proposed --output demo_results. With the default 100-node event generator, ten selected nodes fail at tick 25 and recover at tick 75. Failures may include nonholders, and a random baseline controller failure has an especially large effect. Open summary.csv, then timeseries/node_failures_proposed_timeseries.csv and migrations/node_failures_proposed_migrations.csv. A small run verifies behavior, while the stored 20,000-step experiment addresses longer horizons. Current verification status and actual smoke results appear on the testing slide.

slides.title: Technical challenges and solutions
slides.notes: These challenges are supported by code and development records rather than invented personal anecdotes. Early duplicated role weights motivated the single definition in nodes.py. Separating mesh from hierarchy prevents membership from silently creating radio links. The router separates logical messages from physical hop counts. The development record notes that 20-tick epoch revocation can mask longer lease renewal and batching behavior, leading to configurable retention. Explicit generated-item counts fix denominator ambiguity. A remaining concern is that shared memory gives immediate global capability knowledge unless periodic broadcasts are configured.
rows: Logical hierarchy confused with physical links
Separate logical, hop, and energy counters

slides.title: Testing and validation
body: Regression suites cover configuration, capability, routing, leases, events, metrics, and solar behavior
Edge cases include unreachable routes, invalid transitions, depleted nodes, and delayed recovery
Experiment tests check exported artifacts across scenarios and policies
Fresh execution results are inserted from this review’s verification log
slides.notes: Explain testing by invariant rather than only by count. Arithmetic tests check role weights and normalized aggregation. Router tests verify reliable multihop selection, same-node success, partitions, message counts, and distance energy. Protocol tests cover one assignment per key, hysteresis, renewal at the configured fraction, epoch retention, broadcasts, and recovery delay. Solar tests cover capacity, reproducible rates, reserve recovery, and gate acceptance/rejection. No coverage percentage or runtime benchmark is available. The original history reports 80 tests, while the fresh run is the relevant present result. Fresh test execution: 82 passed in 9.47s. Smoke results: hierarchical: CSC 1.0000, sensor delivery 1.0000; proposed: CSC 1.0000, sensor delivery 1.0000.

slides.title: Stored experimental design
slides.notes: The supplied report declares 480 completed runs: 30 seeds times four scenarios times four arms. Seeds span 42–71 and each run lasts 20,000 ticks. Arms share the initial topology and event schedule within each seed and scenario. The study uses 100 nodes, intercluster gap 1.5 communication ranges, distance energy weight one, hierarchical backhaul, and epoch retention. Moderate harvest is .0002 before the seeded per-node multiplier. Because A and B also differ in controller and selection behavior, B minus A measures a bundled protocol contrast. C minus B isolates harvest within proposed, and D minus C isolates the optional gate.

slides.title: Metric definitions and interpretation
body: CSC = available role-time intervals / required role-time intervals
Default denominator = 56 roles × elapsed ticks, excluding time zero
Sensor delivery = delivered sensor items / generated sensor items
Energy per item = modeled communication energy / delivered sensor items
Lifetime records first threshold crossing and right-censors absent crossings
slides.notes: CSC is a role-state availability proxy. It does not prove that anomaly detection or another application service performed useful computation. Sensor delivery includes unrouted generated items in the denominator, but only online nodes generate traffic, so compare offered load as well as fractions. It also measures the subnet leg rather than root delivery. The stored analyzer uses paired seed differences and 95 percent t intervals. Service lifetime uses cumulative fractions at 90 and 50 percent thresholds, while network lifetime uses instantaneous active-node fraction below 50 percent. Censored horizon values are not observed failure times.

slides.title: Verified stored results: normal scenario
slides.notes: These are per-run means recomputed from the supplied CSV, rounded for display. A retains substantial battery but loses much of the modeled service because coordination can fail. B has much higher role continuity and sensor delivery but low ending battery. C and D reach one in the stored sensor and continuity metrics under this configuration, with higher total communication energy because they sustain service longer. This is not evidence of perfect radio delivery in the field. Fractions are means of run fractions, and energy per item is the mean of per-run ratios, so it need not equal the ratio of displayed means.

slides.title: What the paired comparisons support
body: Normal B − A sensor delivery: +68.02 percentage points
95% paired t interval: +65.68 to +70.35 percentage points
Normal C − B delivery: +16.62 percentage points
Normal D − C delivery: 0.00 percentage points
Normal D − C energy/item: +0.446 × 10⁻⁶ normalized units
slides.notes: Use percentage points for fraction differences. The stored normal B minus A delivery effect is .6801577 with interval [.6568311, .7034843]. C minus B is .1661842 with interval [.1554166, .1769518]. D minus C has zero delivery difference in normal, failures, and energy degradation. In link degradation its delivery interval includes zero. In normal, D slightly increases energy per delivered item, with a positive interval in the stored analysis. Therefore the gate does not establish a general improvement over harvest alone. These intervals describe this paired simulation design and do not establish causality for real devices or universal superiority.

slides.title: Advantages and contributions
body: One shared world supports controlled policy comparisons
Recursive scoring uses the same role vector at every hierarchy level
Explicit lease states make assignment behavior inspectable
Routed traffic and energy expose the cost of coordination
Stored per-seed outputs support further analysis
slides.notes: Frame contributions at the project level. The work integrates deterministic topology, a fixed hierarchy, capability calculations, state machines, policy alternatives, failures, solar energy, and reporting into a small modular simulator. It provides more explanatory value than a score-only demonstration because control exchanges and data routing affect batteries. Its reproducible artifacts are useful for investigating tradeoffs. Avoid claims of patentability, novel scientific priority, or deployment scalability: none follows from this repository alone. The next slide states the boundaries that evaluators are likely to challenge.

slides.title: Limitations
body: Role labels model availability, without anomaly detection or discovery payload algorithms
Shared-memory coordination does not simulate consensus, message delay, or split-brain
No MAC contention, retransmission, sensing / CPU energy, or calibrated radio units
Constant solar rates omit daylight and weather variation
Mesa version drift breaks startup, and SciPy is undeclared
slides.notes: Add several engineering subtleties if asked. Container representation is first available descendant, and initial degree centrality stays fixed. Role availability checks active lease, holder availability, and baseline controller availability, but does not test every application path. Broadcast snapshots default to immediate shared state because interval zero bypasses stale knowledge. Modeled energy counters can exceed actual removed battery energy near zero. The stored study has only one topology-size family and does not prove asymptotic scalability. Missing dependency pinning and an undeclared SciPy requirement reduce environment reproducibility. Fresh verification: Mesa 3.5.1 raises AttributeError when runner.py assigns scenario. Mesa 3.3.1 executes both smoke simulations. This is a concrete compatibility problem caused by the open mesa>=3 requirement, not just a hypothetical risk.

slides.title: Future enhancements
body: Implement real role services with measurable task correctness
Add explicit message queues, delay, partition behavior, and stale-epoch rejection
Measure end-to-end root delivery with a fixed offered-load model
Calibrate radio and battery costs and introduce time-varying solar profiles
Pin dependencies and expand matched scaling and ablation experiments
slides.notes: These are proposals, not existing features. A natural first extension is a service interface per role, separating assignment from service execution and defining useful work. Next introduce asynchronous messages and epoch validation at receivers, then test conflicting holders and network partitions. Track original sensor items through aggregates so root receipt can be measured. Add a realistic energy budget with idle, sensing, and CPU costs. For evaluation, isolate cost awareness, hysteresis, leases, and the gate rather than treating them as one bundle. Test more seeds, node counts, and parameter sensitivities before broad claims.
slides.source: Architectural recommendations based on simulation/ and study design

slides.title: Conclusion and references
body: Implemented: hierarchical capability, role leases, routing, recovery, and solar extensions
Demonstrated: repeatable comparisons with stored 480-run evidence
Main finding: harvest sustains service in this model, while gate benefits remain unproven
Evidence: source code, regression tests, per-run metrics, and paired comparisons
slides.notes: Close by returning to the research question: when is moving a role worth its communication cost? The project gives a reproducible simulation environment to explore that question and makes its assumptions inspectable. The strongest evidence concerns this configured model. Primary internal references are Project.md, FINAL_SPRINT_PLAN.md, SIMULATION_GUIDE.md, nodes.py, simulation modules, tests, and patent-study/results_20000. The stored final report supplies interpretation but the CSVs support the numbers. Library reference names are Mesa, transitions, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, and SciPy. No external papers were supplied or used as evidence. Transition to the appendix for deeper code and viva discussion.

slides.title: Appendix: migration pseudocode
body: current = known_capability(holder, role)
for candidate in available_scope_children:
cost = migration_cost(holder, candidate)
utility = known_capability(candidate, role) - λ * cost
choose candidate with greatest utility above current
if utility > current + Δ and optional_gate_passes:
send MIGRATE, update lease, record change
slides.notes: This is a faithful summary of _consider_cost_aware_migration rather than a direct code quotation. Cooldown can return before the loop. Infinite costs skip unreachable candidates. Adaptive hysteresis adds .15 times one minus mean node energy. The solar gate runs only if a candidate already clears utility and hysteresis. The actual migration control exchange can still fail, in which case the lease does not move. Emergency replacement follows _assign instead of this loop. Distinguish the current capability baseline from candidate utility: the current holder has no new switching penalty.

slides.title: Appendix: complexity and data structures
slides.notes: These are code-derived asymptotic interpretations, not measured benchmarks. Let N be physical nodes, E usable edges, K candidates for one role/scope, and R=4 roles. Topology compares node pairs. Aggregation sorts child IDs and performs weighted sums. Each uncached source builds Dijkstra routes, then materializes each destination path. In a chain the sum of path lengths is quadratic. Caching complete routes for all sources can reach cubic path-node storage in a worst-case graph. Proposed migration scans K candidates and can trigger routes from representatives. This explains why scale tests matter even though default N is only 100.
rows: O(R × Σ k log k) with child sorting
O((N+E) log N + E log N + Σ path lengths)
O(R × scopes), dict of tuple keys
Up to O(N³) stored path-node entries

slides.title: Appendix: configuration and reproducibility
body: Default: seed 42, 100 steps, range 5.2, grid spacing 4.0
Default: epoch 20, leases 10–100, renewal fraction .7, Δ=.05
Study: 20,000 steps, 30 seeds, gap 1.5, distance weight 1
Study: backhaul and valid-lease retention enabled
Verify with Mesa 3.3.1. Mesa 3.5.1 conflicts with model.scenario
slides.notes: Keep default and study configurations separate in your explanation. The basic CLI defaults to five policies and four scenarios, while the study runner defines four particular arms. The initial topology and node attributes are seed-stable and solar randomness uses a separate offset seed. Persisting a run manifest with exact dependency versions and source hash would strengthen reproducibility. The saved NPZ and per-seed CSV files permit inspection without rerunning all 480 long experiments. The code permits configurable broadcasts, cooldown, affected-scope checks, batching, and detection delay, but the study does not enable every option.

slides.title: Viva preparation 1 of 6

body.q: Why separate logical hierarchy from physical mesh?
body.a: Membership defines role candidates and aggregation. Physical adjacency determines whether their representatives can actually communicate.

body.q: How many assignments does the default world require?
body.a: Four roles across ten subnet, three network, and one internetwork scopes: 4 × 14 = 56.

body.q: Does anomaly_detection execute a detection model?
body.a: No. It is a role label scored from energy and health. No anomaly classifier or sensor-payload detector is implemented.

body.q: How are node scores calculated?
body.a: ROLE_WEIGHTS defines normalized weighted sums. Gateway uses .40 energy, .35 link quality, and .25 initial degree centrality.

slides.notes: Use these answers as starting points and point to the named implementation when challenged. Explain assumptions explicitly. If an evaluator asks about measured runtime, radio calibration, deployment security, or statistical coverage beyond these artifacts, state that the repository provides no such evidence. The answers distinguish assignment policy from application service execution and avoid interpreting simulated counters as field measurements.

slides.title: Viva preparation 2 of 6

body.q: What happens to a failed node during aggregation?
body.a: Its capability becomes zero but its child weight remains in the denominator, reducing the parent aggregate.

body.q: Is the root aggregate the global average node score?
body.a: Not necessarily. Default aggregation averages immediate children at each level, and the networks have unequal descendant counts.

body.q: How is a container represented on the physical mesh?
body.a: The first available descendant node in its stored order represents it. This is an abstraction rather than optimized representative election.

body.q: What prevents optional migration oscillation?
body.a: Candidate capability minus weighted migration cost must strictly exceed current capability plus hysteresis. Cooldown and adaptive hysteresis are optional.

slides.title: Viva preparation 3 of 6

body.q: How is migration cost different from charged energy?
body.a: The score cost combines estimated messages, transfer, route-based energy, and disruption. Actual router counters charge the modeled exchanges that execute.

body.q: How do lease renewal and epoch retention interact?
body.a: Renewal updates lease timing at its configured fraction. Without retention, epoch changes regrant leases, potentially occurring before long leases renew.

body.q: Does epoch fencing solve distributed split-brain?
body.a: No. Epoch labels and invalidation operate in one process. Independent receivers, delayed messages, and stale-epoch rejection are not simulated.

body.q: Why does routing sometimes choose more hops?
body.a: Dijkstra minimizes quality-weighted cost, so two reliable edges can cost less than one poor edge.

slides.title: Viva preparation 4 of 6

body.q: When are cached routes invalidated?
body.a: Failure, recovery, link degradation, and depletion invalidate usable graph and source-route caches.

body.q: What is the routing complexity caveat?
body.a: Heap-based shortest paths are followed by explicit reconstruction of every destination path. Path storage can dominate textbook distance-only bounds.

body.q: How is solar energy modeled?
body.a: A constant seeded per-node rate charges batteries up to capacity. Overflow is curtailed, and depleted nodes rejoin after reaching reserve.

body.q: Can the solar gate block failure recovery?
body.a: No. The gate restricts optional migrations. Assignment after holder failure takes the recovery path instead.

slides.title: Viva preparation 5 of 6

body.q: What does CSC measure?
body.a: The fraction of required role-time intervals whose lease and holder satisfy role_available. It excludes time zero and does not prove service-task execution.

body.q: Is sensor delivery measured at the root?
body.a: No. It counts successful sensor items reaching subnet gateways. Optional aggregate backhaul has separate counters.

body.q: Why can high residual energy coexist with poor service?
body.a: A failed controller or unavailable gateway can suppress traffic and leave nodes alive but unable to provide modeled service.

body.q: What does right-censored lifetime mean?
body.a: The threshold did not cross during the observation horizon. The horizon is a bound on observation, not a measured failure time.

body.q: Why compare paired seeds?
body.a: The arms share topology and event schedules for each seed/scenario, reducing unrelated world variation in within-seed differences.

body.q: What does D minus C establish about the gate?
body.a: In the stored study it does not establish an overall delivery or energy-efficiency improvement. Normal delivery is unchanged and energy/item slightly rises.

body.q: What security mechanisms exist?
body.a: Input validation and state consistency checks exist. Authentication, encryption, authorization, and adversarial-node defenses do not.

body.q: What should be improved first?
body.a: Define real role-task execution and end-to-end item delivery, then add asynchronous communication and calibrated energy before deployment claims.
